summary: A battle entry may declare the habitat that holds it, so a cell whose fight is the habitat holder's is encounter-eligible from content alone; the fixture/content equality test then compares encounter_eligible and B6's last Rust-side-only field goes.

coordination.notes: Branched from origin/backend/b0-expedition-state at 2ec3243. Only the battleEntries block of each world cell is touched: lane C5 is adding a dungeonContext block to the same tomb files, so the hunks do not meet. expedition.rs, strategy/ and godot_bridge.rs are untouched -- the fight at a habitat-bound entry is the existing begin_encounter habitat path, not a second spawn rule. Shipped: `AuthoredBattleEntry` (id, status, habitatId with the wire alias habitat_id) is the authored battle-entry shape; `AuthoredCell.battle_entries` replaces the `encounter_eligible` bool the port used to compute, and `AuthoredCell::encounter_eligible` -- an entry is live when its status is `vertical_slice_encounter` or it names a habitat -- is the whole rule, with one owner in Rust instead of half of it in GDScript. `habitat_id` is deliberately NOT carried into `CellDefinition`/`LocationRecord`: which habitat covers a cell is already answered by `HabitatRecord.territory_location_ids`, and a second copy of that answer would drift; `begin_encounter` is untouched, so the fight at a habitat-bound entry is the existing habitat path and there is no second spawn rule. Content authors the binding on tomb_service_passage (status future_spawn_socket -> habitat_holder) and on reception_terrace, whose one-time razorbeak stands on the same precinct's ground; processional_ramp is precinct territory too but carries no habitatId, because the fixture leaves it encounter-ineligible and authoring one would have changed D3's map rather than described it. CHOICE ON HABITAT IDs, per the card: no `content/habitats/` mirror was authored; `habitat.` joins `skill.enemy.` in the validator's `intentionallyExternalPrefixes` instead. A habitat record is mostly its roster, and the roster names creature definition IDs content does not declare -- `enemy.boar.thunderback` and `enemy.raptor.razorbeak.crested` exist nowhere in content/enemies/, and the seven records that do exist carry a `.prototype` suffix the registry does not use -- so an honest twin would first have to invent those creatures, and a half-record that omits the roster would answer "what is a habitat" differently from the registry. That is the card's "cannot be authored honestly" escape. What replaces the validator's reference check is stronger than a prefix allowance: fixture_matches_the_authored_world_cells now fails unless every authored habitatId names a habitat `Habitats::black_beach_vertical_slice()` actually has AND that habitat's territory covers the cell binding it. A `content/habitats/` twin held equal to the registry remains the right end state and is blocked on content/enemies/ growing the two missing creatures and settling the `.prototype` suffix.
